Rashi on Sotah 26b:10:1.english: The hire of a prostitute - He gave a lamb as her hire.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:10:2.english: The price of a dog - He exchanged a dog for a lamb.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:11:1.hebrew: אתנן כלב - שאם אדם אומר לזונה היליך טלה והבעלי לכלבי:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:11:1.english: The payment of a dog - For if a person says to a prostitute, "Here is a lamb for you, in exchange for your having relations with my dog":

Rashi on Sotah 26b:11:2.hebrew: מחיר זונה - היתה לו שפחה זונה, והחליפה בטלה. ומדקאמר "אתנן כלב מותר", מכלל דלאו זנות הוא, דאי זנות הוא, הוה חייל עלה שם אתנן:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:11:2.english: The price of a harlot - He had a maidservant who was a harlot, and he exchanged her for a lamb. And from the fact that [the verse] says "the hire of a dog" is permitted, it follows that [the dog's act] is not [considered] harlotry; for if it were harlotry, the name "hire" would take effect upon it.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:12:1.hebrew: ואלא שכבת זרע למה לי - כיון דאמרת מקנין על ידי שחוף:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:12:1.english: But then, why do I need "seminal emission"? - Since you said that one may warn [a woman] through a shachuf [a man whose organ is damaged].

Rashi on Sotah 26b:13:1.english: In a case where he warned her about [relations] not in the natural manner - [That is, he said to her:] Do not seclude yourself with him to be had [by him] in an unnatural manner.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:13:2.hebrew: משכבי אשה כתיב - הוקשו שני משכבותיה לכל דברים. וכיון דנאסרת עליו, אמאי לא הוי קינוי:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:13:2.english: "The lyings of a woman" is written - Her two lyings [that with her husband and that with the adulterer] are equated for all purposes. And since she becomes forbidden to him, why is it not a [valid] warning?

Rashi on Sotah 26b:14:1.hebrew: דרך אברים פריצותא בעלמא הוא - שוכב עמה בקירוב בשר:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:14:1.english: [Relations] by way of limbs is merely licentiousness - He lies with her with the closeness of flesh.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:14:2.hebrew: פריצותא מי קאסר רחמנא - אשה על בעלה בהכי? וכיון דלא מתסרא עליה בהכי, פשיטא דלאו קינוי הוא:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:14:2.english: Does the Merciful One prohibit [mere] promiscuity? - [Does the Torah prohibit] a woman to her husband through this? And since she is not prohibited to him through this, it is obvious that it is not [considered] a warning [that would subject her to the sotah procedure].

Rashi on Sotah 26b:15:1.english: By a kiss - The sun touches that place.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:15:2.hebrew: היינו דאתא קרא למעוטיה - דלא תימא העראה היא:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:15:2.english: This is [the case] that the verse came to exclude - So that you not say that it is [mere] partial penetration.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:15:3.hebrew: אלא למאן דאמר - ביבמות (דף נה:), העראה האמורה בתורה שהיא כגמר ביאה בכל העריות, כדכתיב (ויקרא כ׳:י״ט) "את מקורה הערה, את שארו הערה" — זו נשיקה. מאי איכא למימר? היכי מצית למימר דאתא קרא למעוטה? הלא כגמר ביאה היא לכל דבר, חוץ משפחה חרופה:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:15:3.english: But according to the one who says - In Yevamot (55b), [it is taught that] the "uncovering" (he'ara) mentioned in the Torah is equivalent to the completion of intercourse in the case of all forbidden relations, as it is written (Leviticus 20:19): "He has uncovered (he'era) her source; he has uncovered (he'ara) his near kin." This ["uncovering"] refers to a kiss. What is there to say? How can you say that the verse comes to exclude it? Surely it is like the completion of intercourse in every respect, except for [the case of] a betrothed Canaanite maidservant (shifcha charufa).

Rashi on Sotah 26b:16:1.hebrew: בקפידה דבעל תליא - דכתיב "וקינא" "ובעל". הא חזינן ליה דקפיד, שהרי קינא לה על כך:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:16:1.english: It depends on the husband's displeasure - For it is written, "and he is jealous" (Numbers 5:14), and "the husband" [is mentioned]. Here we see that he is displeased, since he warned her about this.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:1:1.hebrew: מהו דתימא נטמאה נטמאה שני פעמים - אמורים בפרשה, ודרשינן ליה לקמן (סוטה דף כז:): אחד לבעל ואחד לבועל. היכא דמיתסרא אבועל, בהא סתירה משתעי קרא דנוהג בה דין סוטה; אבל הא דאסורה כו':
Rashi on Sotah 26b:1:1.english: What might you have said: "she was defiled," "she was defiled" [stated] twice - These are stated in the passage, and we expound them below (Sotah 27b): one [teaches the prohibition] to the husband and one to the paramour. Where she is forbidden to the paramour, it is with regard to this [case of] seclusion that the verse speaks, in which the law of a sotah applies to her; but this [other case], that she is forbidden, etc.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:1:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - דכי אתא קרא לגופיה אתא, דהיכא דאינו קרוב לה, נאסר עליה על ידי קינוי זה, ולאו למעוטי קרובים אתא:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:1:2.english: It teaches us - That when the verse comes, it comes for its own sake: that where he is not her relative, she becomes forbidden to him through this warning, and it does not come to exclude relatives.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:2:1.english: The Merciful One said “a man” - “And a man lies with her.”

Rashi on Sotah 26b:2:2.hebrew: שחוף - שבשרו נשחף וכלה ויבש, ואין בו כח. ובתורת כהנים בקללות שנינו דוגמתו: יש לך אדם שהוא חולה ומוטל במטה, אבל בשרו שמור עליו. תלמוד לומר "את השחפת" — מלמד שבשרו נשחף:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:2:2.english: Shachuf (wasted) - [This means] that his flesh is wasted away, consumed, and dried up, and there is no strength in him. And in the Torat Kohanim, regarding the curses, we learned something similar: You might have a person who is ill and bedridden, but his flesh is preserved on him. Therefore the verse states, "the wasting disease (shachefet)" — teaching that his flesh is wasted away.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:2:3.hebrew: מקנין על ידו כו' - כמו "והוינן בה, מקנין על ידו פשיטא":
Rashi on Sotah 26b:2:3.english: One may warn through him, etc. - [This is] like [the passage]: "And we discussed it: 'One may warn through him' — this is obvious!"

Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:1.hebrew: ופוסל בתרומה פשיטא - אם הוא אחד מן הפסולים המחללין את האשה, כגון עובד כוכבים, עבד, חלל, נתין וממזר, דקיימא לן בקדושין וביבמות דפסולין האשה בביאתן — "מובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" — כיון שנבעלה למי שזר אצלה, פסלה:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:1.english: And he disqualifies [her] from terumah — this is obvious! - If he is one of the disqualified men who profane a woman, such as a gentile, a slave, a *chalal* (a priest's son born of a forbidden union), a *natin* (a descendant of the Gibeonites), or a *mamzer*, as we hold in Kiddushin and in Yevamot that they disqualify a woman through their intercourse — [as it says,] "and a priest's daughter who will be [married] to a stranger [*ish zar*]" — since she had relations with one who is a stranger to her, he disqualified her.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:2.hebrew: לא יחלל זרעו - מדלא כתיב "לא יחל", דרשינן שני חילולין: אחד לה, ואחד לזרעה:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:2.english: He shall not profane his seed - Since it does not write "he shall not profane [yachel]," we derive two profanations: one for her, and one for her offspring.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:3.hebrew: דאית ליה זרע מחלל את האשה בביאתו, דלית ליה זרע לא יחלל:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:3.english: One who has seed disqualifies the woman through his intercourse; one who does not have seed does not disqualify her.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:4.hebrew: קא משמע לן - שמואל דפוסל שמעינן ליה מהא דאמר: מקנין על ידי שחוף:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:4:4.english: It teaches us - Shmuel's [ruling] that he disqualifies, we learn from this, where it says: one may warn through a *shachuf*.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:7:1.hebrew: ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר וגו' - ומיניה נפקא לן דפסולין פסלי לאשה בביאתן. ומדאפקיה בלשון הויה, נדרוש: דאית ליה הויה, מי שקידושין תופסין בה, כגון ממזר, נתין וחלל — פסלי. אבל עובד כוכבים ועבד, הרי הן כבהמה, וכיון דלית להו הויה, לא נפסלו. עובד כוכבים אין לו קידושין בישראל, דכתיב (ויקרא כ) "איש אשר ינאף את אשת רעהו", ותניא בסנהדרין (דף נב:) "פרט לאשת אחרים", אלמא לית להו אישות. עבד, "עם החמור" כתיב בהו, "עם הדומה לחמור":
Rashi on Sotah 26b:7:1.english: "And a priest's daughter, if she becomes [the wife of] a lay man," etc. - And from it we derive that disqualified [men] disqualify a woman through their intercourse. And since [the verse] expressed it with the language of "becoming" (havayah), we expound: One who has "becoming," meaning one whose betrothal takes effect with her — such as a mamzer, a Nathin, and a chalal — [these] disqualify. But a gentile and a slave are like an animal, and since they have no "becoming," they do not disqualify. A gentile has no betrothal among Jews, as it is written (Leviticus 20): "A man who commits adultery with his fellow's wife," and it was taught in Sanhedrin (52b): "This excludes the wife of [other, non-Jewish] men"; thus, they have no [valid] marriage. A slave — regarding them it is written "with the donkey," [meaning] "with the one who is like a donkey."

Rashi on Sotah 26b:8:1.hebrew: מי שיש לו אלמנות וגירושין בה - הוא דכי אין לה זרע ממנו, ושבה אל בית אביה, מלחם אביה תאכל. דלא פסלה בביאתו. יצא עובד כוכבים ועבד, שאין לו אלמנות וגירושין בה, שלא תפסו לו בה קידושין, וכשמת אין שם אלמנות עליה. וביבמות פריך: אימא לקולא! דמי שיש לו אלמנות וגירושין הוא דכי אית לה זרע לא תיכול, אבל עובד כוכבים ועבד, אפי' אית לה זרע מיניה תיכול. והתם משני לה בהבא על יבמתו. ומיהו שמעינן [ליה מהא] דמקנין ע"י עובד כוכבים:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:8:1.english: One who has [the status of] widowhood and divorce in her - It is he [alone] with respect to whom, when she has no offspring from him and she returns to her father's house, "she shall eat of her father's bread" — for he has not disqualified her by his relations with her. This excludes a gentile and a slave, who have no [status of] widowhood and divorce in her, since betrothal does not take effect for them with her, and when he dies, the designation of widowhood does not apply to her. And in Yevamot [the Gemara] challenges: Say [that it is] a leniency! For [it is only] one who has [the status of] widowhood and divorce [for whom], when she has offspring, she may not eat [terumah]; but with a gentile or a slave, even if she has offspring from him, she may eat. And there [the Gemara] answers this: [the verse refers] to one who has relations with his yevamah. But nevertheless, we learn [this] from here, that one may warn [a woman] through a gentile.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:9:1.hebrew: ואלא - מי שאינו איש, דמתני' למעוטי בהמה:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:9:1.english: But rather - [the term "man" comes to exclude] one who is not a man; for [the Mishnah's exclusion] is to exclude an animal.

Rashi on Sotah 26b:9:2.hebrew: דאין זנות לבהמה - אינה נעשית זונה בבעילת בהמה, ואינה נאסרת על בעלה:
Rashi on Sotah 26b:9:2.english: For there is no harlotry with an animal - She does not become a harlot through intercourse with an animal, and she is not forbidden to her husband.

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:10:1.hebrew: מנא הא מילתא דאמרי רבנן אין זנות לבהמה - ה"ג בפ' כל האסורין (תמורה ל:): מנא הא מילתא דאין זנות לבהמה? אמר ליה: לא נישתמיט קרא, ונכתוב "אתנן זונה וכלב". א"נ הכי: "אתנן כלב" וכו':
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:10:1.english: "From where is this matter that the Rabbis say, 'There is no harlotry for an animal'?" - This is how the text reads in the chapter "Kol HaIssurin" (Temurah 30b): "From where is this matter, that there is no harlotry for an animal?" He said to him: Scripture would not have omitted it, and it would have written "the hire of a harlot and of a dog." Alternatively, it is this way: "the hire of a dog," etc.

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:15:1.hebrew: אלא למאן דאמר העראה זו נשיקה מאי איכא למימר - והיינו שמואל בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נה:), והכא אליביה דשמואל נמי מסקינן. ותימה: אדרבה איפכא מסתברא! למאן דאמר העראה זו נשיקה, וחשיבה ביאה גבי שאר עריות — היינו דאיצטריך קרא הכא למעוטי; אלא למ"ד העראה זו הכנסת עטרה, ולא חשיבה נשיקה גבי שאר עריות — הכא מאי איצטריך למעוטה:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:15:1.english: But according to the one who says that he'arah [partial relations] is a kiss, what can be said? - This is Shmuel, in the chapter "Haba al Yevimto" (Yevamot 55b), and here too we conclude in accordance with Shmuel. And it is astonishing: On the contrary, the opposite seems more reasonable! According to the one who says that he'arah is a kiss, and it is considered intercourse with regard to other forbidden relations — this is why a verse was needed here to exclude it. But according to the one who says that he'arah is the insertion of the corona, and a kiss is not considered [intercourse] with regard to other forbidden relations — here, what was the verse needed to exclude?

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:1:1.hebrew: אבל הא הואיל ואסורה וקיימא אימא לא קא משמע לן - תימה: הא שמעינן לה מאלמנה לכהן גדול, דאסירה וקיימא לבעל, ואפי' הכי איצטריך קרא דכי תשטה אשתו למעוטי, הא לאו הכי הוה שותה. וכן על מה שאמר "איש אמר רחמנא ולא קטן" נראה דדוקא משתיה ממעט לה קרא, אבל נאסרה על ידי בן תשע שנים ויום אחד, אע"פ שאינו איש, שהרי ביאתו פוסלת בתרומה, כדאיתא בפרק אלמנה (יבמות דף סח.), ונסקלת הערוה על ידו, כדאיתא בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נה:), ומקומו בפרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מה.), דומיא דכל עריות מקנא על ידן. דלא איצטריך לאשמועינן אלא דשותות, אבל דנאסרו — פשיטא! וכי משום דעריות נינהו גריעי?:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:1:1.english: "But this one, since she is forbidden and remains [so], say it does not teach us" - This is puzzling: we already learn this from a widow [married] to a High Priest, who is forbidden and remains [forbidden] to her husband, and nevertheless the verse "if his wife goes astray" was needed to exclude [her from drinking]; for otherwise, she would drink. And likewise, regarding what [the Gemara] said, "'Man,' the Merciful One said, and not a minor" — it appears that the verse excludes only her drinking; but she does become forbidden through a nine-year-old and one day, even though he is not a "man," since his intercourse disqualifies [a woman] from terumah, as stated in the chapter Almanah (Yevamot 68a), and the forbidden relation is stoned through him, as stated in the chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 55b), and its source is in the chapter Yotzei Dofen (Niddah 45a); similar to all forbidden relations, [where] one warns [the woman] on account of them. For [the Gemara] needed to teach us only that she drinks, but that they become forbidden is obvious! And is it because they are forbidden relations that they are inferior?

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:2:1.hebrew: שחוף - פירש רבינו חננאל: שאינו בועל כדרכו ואינו מזריע. דתניא: "איזהו מרוח אשך? זה הקליטים, שנכנס רוח באשכיו" — דברי ר"ע. רבי ישמעאל אומר: "זה השחוף". תימה: אמאי נקט שמואל שחוף ולא נקט סריס? ושמא שחוף הוי רבותא טפי:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:2:1.english: A shachuf - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [This is a man] who does not engage in relations in the usual manner and does not emit seed. For it was taught [in a baraita]: "Who is one with a 'wind-affected testicle'? This is the kelitim, whose testicles have had wind enter them" — these are the words of Rabbi Akiva. Rabbi Yishmael says: "This is the shachuf." It is puzzling: Why did Shmuel mention a shachuf and not mention a eunuch (saris)? Perhaps [the case of] a shachuf is a greater novelty.

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:6:1.hebrew: אבל הא הואיל ואסירא וקיימא - תימא: מאי קמ"ל רב הונא? והא מתני' היא: ע"י כל עריות מקנין! וי"ל דהכי פירושו: מי שנאסר בכל בת ישראל ע"י בעילת זנות, אפילו אינה קרובתו — יצא עובד כוכבים, דבלאו הכי כל בת ישראל מתסרא וקיימא לגביה:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:6:1.english: "But this one, since she is forbidden and remains [so]" - One might ask: What is Rav Huna teaching us? Surely this is [stated in] our Mishnah: "Through [a transgression of] any of the forbidden relations, they warn [the wife]"! And one can answer that this is its explanation: One who becomes forbidden to every Jewish woman through an act of intercourse in sin, even if she is not his relative — this excludes a gentile, since even without this, every Jewish woman is forbidden and remains [so] with regard to him.

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:8:1.hebrew: יצא עובד כוכבים שאין לו אלמנות וגירושין בה - פירש רש"י: דנפקא לן מדכתיב "אשר ינאף את אשת רעהו" — פרט לאשת אחרים. תימה, והא נפקא לן בקידושין בפרק האומר: מ"לא תתחתן בם". וכמדומה דלא אתי קרא "פרט לאשת אחרים" אלא למעוטי ישראל הבא על העובדת כוכבים אשת עובד כוכבים, וקמ"ל אע"ג דבעולת בעל יש להן, ישראל בעובדת כוכבים פטור:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:8:1.english: "A gentile is excluded, as he has no widowhood or divorce in it [i.e., in the marriage-based laws of adultery]" - Rashi explained that we derive this from the verse, "Who commits adultery with his fellow's wife," [which excludes] the wife of others. [This is] puzzling, for we derive this in Kiddushin, in the chapter "HaOmer" [from the verse], "You shall not intermarry with them." And it seems that the verse [teaching] "excluding the wife of others" comes only to exclude an Israelite who has relations with a gentile woman who is the wife of a gentile, and it informs us that even though they have [the status of] a woman who has been married (be'ulat ba'al), an Israelite [who has relations] with a gentile woman is exempt.

Tosafot on Sotah 26b:9:1.hebrew: למעוטי בהמה - תימה: דהכא משמע דבזנות תליא מילתא. אם כן, רבא דאמר בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף נד.) דיש זנות לבהמה, מתני' למעוטי מאי? וכי אית לן למימר דל"ל דשמואל או דרב הונא:
Tosafot on Sotah 26b:9:1.english: To exclude an animal - This is puzzling: for here it implies that the matter depends on [the concept of] licentiousness (zenut). If so, [consider] Rava, who said in the chapter "HaBa al Yevamto" (Yevamot 54a) that there is [the concept of] zenut with an animal — what, then, is the Mishnah excluding? Are we really to say that [Rava] does not [hold] like Shmuel or Rav Huna?
